title: Adventures in mental time travel
coreMove: Let a future review point inspect today before the present mood spends the chips.
sourcePressure: The source support is thinner here, so the plan stays narrow: mental time travel widens present judgment through future review, 10-10-10 thinking, premortems, backcasting, and regret placed before commitment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must state that future perspective widens the frame; it does not reveal the future or guarantee regret-free decisions.

sourceAnchors.name: 10-10-10 thinking
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source names 10-10-10 thinking as one tool for widening the time frame of a decision.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Ten minutes, ten months, and ten years can each ask a different question of the same impulse.

sourceAnchors.name: premortems and backcasting
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source lists premortems and backcasting as future-facing checks that bring later review into present choice.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A premortem lets a later failure speak early enough to change the plan.

sourceAnchors.name: regret moved before the decision
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source says regret is more useful when moved in front of the choice rather than processed only afterward.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Regret is a better tool before the signature than after the apology.

examples: journal entry split then and now

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: home renovation contract before signing a change order
exampleSpecs.stakes: current frustration could approve a costly shortcut that looks foolish by final inspection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask Megan to read the change order as if the inspector is already standing in the finished kitchen three months from now.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You have a pen over the change order while drywall dust sits on the counter.

exampleSpecs.domain: city marathon permit decision during a heat-warning week
exampleSpecs.stakes: present pressure from sponsors could crowd out the later safety review
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "What will the incident report ask us first?" Julien says, moving the discussion from sponsor pressure to the later safety file.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "What will the incident report ask us first?" Julien says, with the heat bulletin open.

exampleSpecs.domain: startup acquisition term sheet with a fast deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: a celebratory offer could hide terms future employees will resent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:35 p.m., Kasia backcasts from the first all-hands after acquisition and marks which terms would be hardest to defend then.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:35 p.m., Kasia puts the champagne back in the mini-fridge and opens the vesting schedule.

exampleSpecs.domain: college major selection before a scholarship deadline
exampleSpecs.stakes: family pressure and deadline panic may narrow the view of future coursework and debt
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What would Ben ask after two semesters of the major, with the scholarship used and the first lab grade posted?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would the second-semester version of Ben ask that deadline-night Ben is avoiding?

exampleSpecs.domain: elder-care move decision after one frightening fall
exampleSpecs.audience: adult children making family care decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: fear from the latest fall could rush a move that needs a wider view of health, autonomy, and support
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid runs a premortem for both choices, naming what each future regret would accuse today of ignoring.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The hallway night-light is still on at noon after the ambulance leaves.

exampleSpecs.domain: film festival jury choosing a controversial prize winner
exampleSpecs.stakes: present-room momentum may choose the safest film instead of the one the jury can defend later
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego asks the jury to write the award note from one year later before the vote, exposing which choice survives distance.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Diego one festival cycle to learn that applause in the room fades faster than the printed award note.

skillTargets: use future review without claiming foresight
identify present bias in urgent decisions

tryThisNowSpec: Before one decision today, write three review questions from a later vantage point: ten minutes after, ten months after, and when the first hard evidence arrives.
